Event: `d0cb03a84e1c104c582d9867a502df8c` · 2026-09-24T20:28:02Z

> Red-team code review, checkpoint 2: 2f5762b2e and ce95d19ba. Code reading in a scratch worktree at ce95d19ba, now removed. I did not re-run the boot cases; the implementer reports all PASS on rv64 and rv32.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK for merge on P1-1 (a small fix; commit 5 work can continue). Everything else is OK with notes.
> 
> P1-1 Budget-deadline deferral is keyed on PREVIOUS_PAIR, which the legacy ReturnToParent call sets outside any callback.
> - time.rs defers budget deadlines while arch::irq::in_callback(), which is PREVIOUS_PAIR.is_some() (irq.rs:88).
> - The legacy SysCall::ReturnToParent handler (syscall.rs:1040) calls set_isr_return_pair whenever SWITCHTO_CALLER is Some, which it normally is for any process kmain switched to. The legacy interface is served to every U-mode process, Redoubt-created ones included, with no gating, and nothing clears the pair without a real interrupt (finish_isr returns early unless HANDLING_IRQ).
> - By code reading, any process can therefore put the kernel into 'callback' mode indefinitely. Every budget deadline in the system is deferred (rearm arms only timeouts), so WP-K5's 'a deadline destroys its budget' is defeated, including for the caller's own lease.
> - Two pre-existing effects of the same state make it worse: redoubt::handle's in_irq makes every Redoubt call NotPermitted for every process (so the steward's budget_destroy is refused too: TENETS 3), and a later legacy Yield hits do_yield's expect on SWITCHTO_CALLER (a kernel panic, I14).
> Fix, in K5 since it owns the kernel:
> (a) key the deferral, and redoubt's in_irq, on the real callback state (HANDLING_IRQ, set only when the kernel starts a callback), not on PREVIOUS_PAIR;
> (b) refuse ReturnToParent from user processes (the SWITCHTO_CALLER comment says the mechanism is unused), or remove it with the other dead Xous scheduling calls.
> Add an attack case asserting that a process which makes the legacy call is still destroyed at its lease deadline, and that Redoubt calls keep working for everyone else.
> 
> Verified OK:
> - Entry protocol. Every trap except CallFromSMode (kmain's SwitchTo) expires first, then re-reads current: if the entering pid changed or its slot is free, it resumes current. PREVIOUS_PAIR, the syscall paths and faulted() all run after that check, so none sees a dead pid. kmain expires, picks and switches with no entry in between, a failed SwitchTo resets SWITCHTO_CALLER and re-picks, and its expect is gone. Idle-window S-mode timer and IRQ entries expire with running() = None. The SupervisorTimerInterrupt branch only rearms.
> - Deadline list integrity. Word 15 was unused before (checked at 7aedd10d6). new_budget writes it as None, then links; the budget_create failure path unlinks before freeing. destroy_marked unlinks each dying frame before freeing it, in ascending frame order, and the predecessor walk only ever touches live or not-yet-freed frames, so it is correct for head, middle and chains of dying nodes. No other path frees a budget frame. A descendant destroyed with its ancestor is gone from the list before its own deadline is looked up.
> - Order. Timeouts come before budgets at an equal instant (td <= bd); budgets by (deadline, id); timeouts by (deadline, then walk order (pid, tid)). now is fixed per call, so work per entry is bounded, and anything later is re-armed (an immediate interrupt if already past).
> - The deadline path's caller is running() (none for PID 1). destroy_subtree kills it last and returns caller_doomed, and a process killed through budgets_dying (its object charged to the subtree) is caught by the trap's re-read.
> - Arithmetic on both widths: us_to_ticks rounds up (frac x hz < 2^52, checked secs x hz), ticks_to_us floors and saturates, and set() adds BOOT_TICKS with a checked add. Boot fails closed without Time.
> - IRQ 0: interrupt_claim(0) is InterruptNotFound, the timer ops return UnhandledSyscall, irq-attack asserts both, and timer, timer-test and the constants are gone.
> - The icount option is purely additive (Option, default None; adds '-icount <s> -rtc clock=vm' only when set), so existing cases are unchanged.
> 
> Reply race (implementer's item 2): acceptable, and it matches the IPC completion row 'taken call times out: Later discarded, mask 0'. A reply entering after the timeout finds F_WAITING clear, gets discarded and closes the call, and the owed notice goes with it. That is pre-existing semantics (the caller-death race behaves the same way); the timer only makes it reachable without a second process. But I15 says 'reported ... exactly once'. P3: have the K5 docs commit state that when the reply wins the race, the discarded result is the report and no notice follows, so I15 and the model read the same.
> 
> finish_isr's expect (item 3): sound once P1-1 is fixed. With deferral keyed on a real callback, nothing kills the previous pair during one: Redoubt calls are refused in_irq, legacy calls are limited to can_call_from_interrupt, and timeouts only wake. As it stands, P1-1's stale pair (pid 1) is the one way in.
> 
> R10 cost (item 1): the relative assertion (lateness <= a hand destroy of the same shape + 1 ms) is sound for what it tests, timer latency. Two notes:
> (a) About 21 ms of virtual time per destroy is non-preemptible kernel time (SIE clear). It delays every interrupt and timeout on the machine, and it will show up directly in sched-latency's driver-wake p99/max whenever a lease ends. Record destroy duration as its own column in the latency table and set the target knowing it.
> (b) The cost scales with object frames (mark_dying and destroy_marked scan 0..high_frame; budgets_dying's find-from-0 loops are O(E x F)), which any budget can grow with its pages, so it inflates everyone's destroys. Yes, make it a tracked follow-up (per-subtree indexes for budgets and endpoints), not K5.
> 
> P3:
> 1. Deferred budget deadlines are re-armed only on the RETURN_FROM_ISR path. A callback that ends through EXIT_THREAD or a fault calls finish_isr without expiring or rearming, so a due deadline waits for the next entry. Call rearm (or expire) after every finish_isr.
> 2. Budget deferral during a genuine callback is unbounded: a callback that never returns holds every deadline, not only the CPU. It is the stated residual until K6, but state it as 'all deadlines', and note that grants are keyed by PID (grants.rs), so check that a Redoubt-created process that reuses a granted boot process's PID cannot inherit its legacy IRQ grant.
> 3. all-together now runs no program that arms the timer (log-server and ipc-client never block with a timeout), so it no longer covers timer/IPC interference under smp 1/2. Add a sleeper to it.
> 4. expire_due walks every thread once per due timeout (O(k x T) per entry), not the one shared walk the plan describes. That is fine for now; revisit with commit 5's billing.
> 5. Read sstatus.SPP before expire_at_entry rather than after. Nothing in expiry changes it today, but the check depends on that.

> P3s: rearm after every finish_isr; confirm PID-keyed grants can't be inherited via PID reuse while deferral applies; restore timer coverage in all-together (a timeout sub-case); expiry walks per item; read SPP before expiry.
